title: Gain-aware calibration for a selected elastic mode
status: open project subproblem; review proposal only
statement: Identify the smallest useful calibrated data set for log(E), log(rho), log(g) in a fixed-geometry single-mode sphere/receptance model and quantify conditioning under declared measurement uncertainty.
assumptions: Known radius, Poisson ratio and damping within the benchmark
Homogeneous isotropic linear material and matched mode
g is one combined positive frequency-independent input/readout gain
Data include selected frequency and nonzero off-resonance magnitude; calibrated mass is an additional candidate measurement
unresolvedGap: Previous scaling/kernel result does not give a gain-aware calibration uncertainty budget or test drift/model mismatch.
feasibleNow: Existing production sphere and FRF functions plus independent roots and complex solves; only three declared log parameters.
modelVsHardware: Synthetic identifiability and calibration design only; no calibrated sensor or specimen data exist. Separate input and receiver gains remain indistinguishable without another reference.
negativeControls: (E,rho,g) to (aE,a*rho,a*g) leaves frequency and raw response unchanged
Duplicated channels do not increase rank
Frequency-dependent gain must defeat a constant-gain fit
Known density removes only the declared two-material-parameter ambiguity
deliverable: Exact parameter/observable map, kernel/rank conditions, frozen synthetic benchmark specification and uncertainty/calibration budget.
dependencies: Explicit noise and calibration model selected during planning
candidateFutureCode: An isolated new calibration benchmark; no change proposed to accepted old outputs

sourceReadingDepth.depth: Full own derivation and results; independent skeptic cross-review received
Entire short scope page; associated manuscript pp.1–3 and Theorem1.1 previously read; no proof or Lean audit

title: Position-comparison pole estimator under nuisance changes
status: open project subproblem; review proposal only
statement: Determine when selected finite transfer data distinguish a controlled sphere-pole perturbation from support, gain, temperature and mode-visibility changes in the declared two-mode model, including an abstention outcome.
assumptions: Selected frequency band and explicitly matched modes
Linear passive forward fixture; support and receiver parameters tracked
Conventional low-order estimator and frozen mode-selection rules
No claim that modeled pole attribution is unique outside the declared model
unresolvedGap: Forward plots and finite FFT checks exist, but the current tool record has no accepted noisy pole-fit benchmark for A/B/A or ABBA comparisons.
feasibleNow: Existing coupledSystem/responseAt, synthetic acquisition and verified pyFRF adapter provide independent forward and spectral baselines.
modelVsHardware: First validate estimator behavior on synthetic records; later hardware sample size and uncertainty require pilot data. Existing experimental protocol is proposed, not performed.
negativeControls: Gain-only change and nodal mode suppression
Unchanged intrinsic sphere with changed contact stiffness
Indistinguishable nuisance-only alternative must trigger ambiguity
Empty-table subtraction is not exact decoupling
positiveControl: Known sphere-parameter perturbation with declared matched-mode identity; recovery must be qualified by possible nuisance alternatives.
deliverable: Frozen estimator benchmark with confusion/abstention schema and an updated preregistration for the existing position protocol.
dependencies: Declared estimator, noise and model-discrepancy families
candidateFutureCode: Existing tool-bench interfaces; no accepted pyEMA fit assumed

sourceReadingDepth.depth: Synthetic tool checks and unexecuted-model list
Primary page re-opened; prior §§1–3.2 including reciprocity and Helmholtz model; no trained model run

nonClaims: No physical location-dependent intrinsic frequency found
No preselected hardware effect size or statistical power

title: Minimum independent ports within a finite candidate model
status: conditional optional project subproblem; review proposal only
statement: Enumerate a finite candidate source/receiver menu for a fixed truncated passive model and identify the smallest subset meeting a declared normalized rank/conditioning criterion over a chosen band.
assumptions: Fixed finite mode truncation and candidate port menu
Known units and noise normalization for singular values
Gain model fixed or independently calibrated
Minimality restricted to enumerated menu and declared criterion
unresolvedGap: Duplicate inputs were shown nonidentifying, but no selected port layout has been tested for hidden modes, weak coupling, symmetry and practical conditioning.
feasibleNow: Small-matrix exhaustive subset enumeration is bounded; existing finite forward models and independent NumPy solves suffice.
modelVsHardware: Model candidate layout only; real geometry, mode shapes, calibration and omitted modes require separate validation. Finite rank cannot certify a continuum boundary operator.
negativeControls: Changed candidate menu invalidates unqualified minimum claim
deliverable: Port-selection contract, machine-readable rank/nullity/singular-value table, held-out source/receiver checks and explicit rejected-layout kernels.
